extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs, Department of the Interior, Indian agents and superintendents
extracted.subtask_description: Annual field report from a U.S. Indian agent describing reservation administration, agriculture, schools, policing, sanitary conditions, and recommended actions for improving Indian agency welfare and governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allotment of land in severalty / partitioning to heads of families
rubrics_metrics.description: Allotments made in fee and practically partitioned to heads of families impart additional incentives to industry and have improved condition of farms, comforts, and prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Tuscaroras' land held in common but practically partitioned; Cornplanter and other allotments led to greater industry. Allotment and extinction of tribal relations are credited with reducing jealousies and producing permanent improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on sale of allotted lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Where allotments are made, sales may be limited by statute or commission (e.g., commissioners appointed with power to sell only to Senecas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such sale restrictions are presented as a protective measure to secure the benefits of allotment while guarding against outside acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-bribery protections for Indian nation officers
rubrics_metrics.description: "An act to prevent the bribing and corrupting of officers of the Seneca Nation of Indians" — penalizes white persons offering bribes to Seneca officers and Indian officers who accept bribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties specified: white persons — imprisonment not over five years or fine up to $1,000 or both; Indian officers accepting bribes — imprisonment not exceeding one year or fine not exceeding $200. The Seneca general council approved the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extinguish pre-emption/clouds on title to enable partition and improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Clouds on title (e.g., Ogden Land Company pre-emption claim) prevent partition of lands in severalty and paralyze industry and improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: use of annuity funds or other means to extinguish such claims to remove barriers to partition and economic development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lease income per council orders for nation debts and expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Income from leasing reservation village lands is to be paid to the nation treasurer and distributed upon orders of the Seneca council to pay debts and current government expenses of the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model: Seneca Nation leases produce ~ $10,000 annually and council-controlled disbursement is used to meet nation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit sale of all intoxicating beverages to Indians (including cider/beer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Traffic in hard cider (often disguised) and other intoxicants is a principal source of intemperance and demoralization among Indians; proposed statutory amendment to include cider and beer that intoxicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend section 2139 of the U.S. Statutes to prohibit sale to Indians of all intoxicating beverages, citing effects: quarrels, breaches of peace, demoralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for Indians to perform government hauling and transportation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indians have hauled government supplies effectively and at lower cost; they should be allowed preference in performing hauling work if they desire it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: hauling done at small expense (e.g., $50 worth of supplies), and elsewhere 100 tons transported at $10 per ton by Indian teams vs. more than double by contractors — employment benefit and departmental savings cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of agricultural machinery and implements (thrasher, reaper, oxen)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government should furnish new threshers, reapers, oxen, and implements when agency machines are worn out to enable Indians to perform harvest work within short favorable climate periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: existing machines (5–6 years' use) become useless; new equipment and oxen expand acreage under cultivation and increase yields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage agricultural practices such as summer fallow and crop diversification
rubrics_metrics.description: Constant seeding with the same kinds of grain and indifferent farm work cause foul fields and poor yields; summer fallow and better practices are recommended to improve crops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Barrier: Indians often too poor or have too little land to fallow; recommendation implies governmental assistance (seed, implements, temporary rations) may be needed to allow fallowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency farm development to supply breadstuffs and support occupants
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency farms should be brought into cultivation (fencing, plowing) to produce wheat, oats, and other staples sufficient to feed reservation occupants and boarding schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Malheur agency produced 2,400 bushels wheat and 1,900 bushels oats and was able to supply breadstuffs for occupants when properly expanded and equipped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey and settle reservation boundaries to prevent disputes and encroachments
rubrics_metrics.description: New surveys are needed to settle boundaries beyond dispute; unsettled lines are a source of difficulties between Indians and whites and may lead to serious trouble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: authorities should take action to remove grounds for dissension caused by boundary complications, which also enable encroachment by cattle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforce penalties against grazing encroachments and pursue legal remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Stock-men encroaching on reservation grazing lands should be prosecuted and made to pay penalties; several cases resulted in fines/judgments, though enforcement faces obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed problems: juries reluctant to punish settlers when Indians are absent; some cases failed for want of testimony; federal attorneys sometimes do not proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize and maintain Indian-elected local justice system for minor offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor offenses may be tried by Indian justices of the peace (elected annually) with or without jury; Indian sheriff and prosecuting attorney can effectively enforce discipline without government expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At some agencies this system proved successful and satisfactory as an inexpensive enforcement mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize agency police force and detention with manual labor sentencing
rubrics_metrics.description: A police force (captain, sergeants, men, with a white chief) and suitable cells for confinement where prisoners serve sentences by manual labor is effective and salutary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Klamath agency built cells accommodating eight prisoners; the system had a salutary effect upon evil-doers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and expand boarding schools and day schools with adequate facilities and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Boarding-school improvements (dining-room, schoolroom, dormitories) and regular contracted teachers lead to increased attendance and satisfactory progress in studies and industrial habits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: new schoolrooms and dining facilities; contracted teachers (religious societies) sustaining schools; boarding-school houses accommodating 60–75 children improved educational reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish hospital facilities to improve sanitary conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A good hospital building with suitable furnishings and supplies for eight to ten patients is needed to improve sanitary conditions and reduce reliance on native doctors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a hospital would break up native practice, destroy its influence, and materially raise health standards and population growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorize Indians to maintain public roads and collect reasonable tolls for revenue and employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing Indians to keep certain roads in repair during summer months and charge reasonable tolls would provide revenue, induce labor, and accommodate the traveling public without obvious evil results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a road formerly owned by a company has been abandoned and could economically employ Indians to maintain it and collect tolls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer returning displaced/banished Indians to their agency where unjustly exiled
rubrics_metrics.description: Where bands (e.g., Chief Leggins' people) were banished unjustly, their safe return and restoration of rights is a moral imperative to prevent lasting resentment and potential violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument framed as a solemn question of right and wrong rather than policy; returning such groups may be necessary for reconciliation and stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure accountability and recovery of missing agency public property
rubrics_metrics.description: Public property removed by military or other custodians must be accounted for and recovered; failure to do so leaves agencies deprived of necessary equipment and supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: missing lumber, flour, platform scales, galvanic battery; military transfers and legal obstacles thwart recovery; recommend administrative/legal actions to resolve accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect and accept annuity supplies of good quality and suspend further shipments when unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Annuity supplies purchased for Indian agencies should be examined for quality; if supplies are already abundant at an agency, further shipments should be withheld until needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Malheur agency stores crowded with supplies; recommendation to stop sending additional supplies until return of Indians is decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage taking new lands and permanent home-building to secure improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouraging Indian families to take lands, build houses and barns, and secure permanent homes is favorable to future progress and prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government support (oxen, implements, fencing lumber, wire) helps open new territory and increases acreage under cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address and adjudicate spoliation (raid) claims before Congress for prompt examination and payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for property destroyed during raids should be examined and brought before Congress for necessary legislation to secure prompt examination and speedy payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: four spoliation claims aggregating $14,357.76 recommended for Congressional action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combat venereal and hereditary diseases through skilled medical attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Reservation populations suffer from long-term venereal diseases contracted historically; eradication requires years of skilled attention and medical care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical note: high numbers of births and deaths attributed to such diseases; sustained medical intervention required.
